correctness.rationale: The polygon is parametrized by all positive diagonal half-lengths. The established convex-curve halving-chord theorem reduces dilation to a complete piecewise-quadratic chord minimization; every interval and possible unconstrained stationary point is accounted for via the identity G-F=ps(p+r)(s-t)>=0. The two analytic expressions agree algebraically in angular variables. The profile f has strictly increasing derivative of log f in beta, its optimized profile is strictly decreasing in alpha, and sec alpha is strictly increasing; exact bracketing and the interior stationary equation prove a single global optimum. An independently implemented chord-by-chord algorithm agreed on 1000 diverse kites within 5.28e-16 relative error; finite checks are supplementary, not universal proof.

originality.rationale: The full accessible foundational proofs furnish the halving-chord method and generic polygon bounds, but their theorems do not imply a two-mode explicit dilation formula for every asymmetric kite nor the sharp unique kite optimizer. The best all-four-gon bound from the inspected papers is 4 tan(pi/8), strictly below the claimed sharp 1.9237956679..., while the centrally symmetric theorem applies only to rhombi and gives 2. The independently derived shape minimization is not an instance of these already-established inequalities. value.rationale: Geometric dilation measures worst detour along a boundary and is a central invariant in convex-curve and geometric-network analysis. The all-kite two-mode formula determines when fundamentally different perimeter-halving chords govern the stretch factor. Its non-obvious sharp universal optimizer is unique and asymmetric, improving the square/rhombus reference value 2 to approximately 1.92379567. This is a complete natural-family classification with an explicit sharp constant, not a routine parameter substitution or a known-table recomputation.
